facts.businessDescription: Meridian Flow Systems builds inline water-monitoring hardware and the software that runs it for industrial plants and water utilities. Sensor probes measure flow, pressure, turbidity and conductivity; a rugged edge unit collects the data on-site and pushes it into the Meridian dashboard, alerting plant engineers before thresholds are breached.
facts.idealClientProfile: Operations and process engineers at food and beverage plants, breweries, municipal water utilities and industrial laundries. Decision makers: plant manager, operations director, quality lead. Website purpose: book a monitoring assessment call.
extraInformation: Positioning: engineered, precise, unglamorous in the best way. Supporting message: instrumentation you can trust, from probe to dashboard.

Product line (exactly these four): Sensor probes — inline flow, pressure, turbidity and conductivity probes built for continuous industrial service. MF-Edge unit — a rugged on-site collector that buffers data during outages and pushes to the dashboard when the link returns. Meridian dashboard — thresholds, trends and export; built for plant engineers, not data scientists. Assessment & install — site survey, probe placement planning, installation and calibration by the company's own engineers.

Process, four stages: 01 Survey — map the process line and define measurement points. 02 Instrument — specify probes and edge unit placement. 03 Install & calibrate — fitting, calibration and threshold setup. 04 Monitor — dashboard onboarding and alert tuning with the plant team.
Things to emphasize: measurement accuracy, buffer-then-forward reliability during network outages, engineers who install and calibrate in person.
Strict content constraints: do not invent customers, case studies, uptime percentages, accuracy specs, certifications, awards, pricing or headcount. Describe capabilities without quantitative claims.

creativeDirection.direction: Precision instrument: a technical, engineered aesthetic — cool slate surfaces with a signal-amber accent, a visible layout grid like graph paper, monospaced data labels, schematic line diagrams as section dividers, and dense, well-considered typography that respects the reader
creativeDirection.audience: Operations and process engineers; technical buyers who distrust marketing fluff
creativeDirection.serviceEnvironment: Industrial plant floors and utility rooms: stainless pipe, control cabinets, cable runs, status LEDs
creativeDirection.preferredPalette: Slate #22272B, cool steel #E8ECEF, signal amber #E8A020, deep teal #1F5F5B, ink black #14171A
creativeDirection.visualStyle: Engineering drawing meets modern spec sheet: visible hairline grid, section numbers like drawing codes (01/, 02/), monospaced labels for data and part names, restrained photography of hardware in real plant environments
creativeDirection.tone: Exact, calm, competent; no adjectives where a measurement belongs
creativeDirection.avoidances: No generic SaaS dashboard screenshots, no stock handshakes or hard hats, no rounded friendly cards, no decorative gradients, no invented metrics or up-time claims
creativeDirection.inspirationNotes: P&ID schematics, DIN rail layouts, calibration certificates, machined aluminum faceplates
